what_it_does: 5G and satellite systems need very pure radio signals at specific frequencies to work reliably. This paper describes a special oscillator (a circuit that generates these pure signals) that works at millimeter-wave frequencies (47-58 GHz, much higher than typical phone signals). The oscillator uses a design called Colpitts with a transformer, which shapes the radio wave more efficiently and reduces unwanted noise. Built in 40-nanometer silicon, it achieves exceptionally high spectral purity—about 10 decibels better than previous designs at the same frequency range.
